cards.q: What are the two multicast control mechanisms covered here?
cards.a: Multicast boundaries restrict how far multicast can propagate (scoping with TTL thresholds and group ACLs), and the RPF check ensures a loop-free source-rooted tree by only forwarding packets that arrive on the unicast interface toward the source.

cards.q: What is the RPF check in multicast?
cards.a: RPF (Reverse Path Forwarding) forwards a multicast packet only if it arrived on the interface the unicast routing table would use to reach the source; otherwise the packet is dropped as an RPF failure.

cards.q: What does the RPF check use as its basis?
cards.a: RPF uses the existing unicast routing table (RIB); multicast itself does not maintain a separate topology, so the source-facing interface is derived from unicast routing.

cards.q: What happens to a multicast packet that fails the RPF check?
cards.a: It is silently dropped, since it arrived on an interface the unicast RIB does not point toward the source; this silent drop is a common multicast troubleshooting symptom.

cards.q: How does asymmetric unicast routing affect RPF?
cards.a: Asymmetric routing sends the multicast packet back on a non-RPF interface, causing an RPF failure; it is fixed with MBGP alternate paths, static RPF routes, or tunnels that align the RPF path.

cards.q: What are the types of multicast boundaries?
cards.a: A TTL boundary using ip multicast ttl-threshold, a group boundary using ip multicast boundary with an ACL, administratively scoped 239/8 groups, and Auto-RP scope limiting the 224.0.1.39/40 group propagation.
It is reserved for administratively scoped multicast, meaning group traffic in this range is never forwarded beyond the local domain.

cards.q: Which commands verify RPF and boundaries?
cards.a: show ip rpf, show ip mroute, show ip pim interface, debug ip mpacket, and show ip igmp interface.

cards.q: Multicast packets are being dropped despite receivers being present; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: An RPF failure is likely: the packet is arriving on a different interface than the unicast RIB points toward the source, so it is silently dropped; check show ip rpf for the source.

cards.q: What is the difference between an RPF check and a multicast boundary?
cards.a: RPF decides whether to forward based on the source-facing interface (loop prevention), while a boundary decides how far multicast may travel using TTL thresholds and group ACLs (scoping).

cards.q: What is the boundaries and RPF quick-review summary?
cards.a: RPF forwards only packets arriving on the unicast-RIB source-facing interface and silently drops others to prevent loops, while TTL and group boundaries plus the 239/8 admin scope confine multicast propagation, with MBGP or static routes fixing asymmetric RPF.
